description: A login form builds a SQL query by directly concatenating the username and password fields into a WHERE clause, with no parameterization.
explanation: Because the query is built with raw string concatenation, input isn't treated as data -- it's treated as part of the SQL syntax itself. A username of something like `' OR '1'='1' --` closes the intended string literal early, injects an always-true condition, and comments out the rest of the query (including the password check), so the query matches the first row in the table regardless of what password was supplied.
solve_steps: Try a single quote in the username field and watch for a SQL error -- confirms the field is unescaped
Try `' OR '1'='1' --` (or `' OR 1=1 -- -` depending on the DB's comment syntax) as the username with any password
If that doesn't return an admin session specifically, add an ORDER BY / row-targeting condition, e.g. `' OR username='admin' --`
Confirm the resulting session belongs to the intended account
notes: If quotes are filtered, check whether the query uses numeric context (no quotes needed) or try encoding tricks before assuming the field is actually safe.
